article.name: Agents Remember
article.summary: Agents Remember gives coding agents a Git-versioned knowledge tree with source-path cards, structured records and a workflow that checks recorded knowledge against code changes. The reviewed source describes repository-scoped memory, a derived read index, Curator-authored updates and bounded path or record reads.

who_what.text: The official README presents Agents Remember as a Git-backed memory and change-review product for coding agents. The repository describes a Python package with an MCP tool server and dashboard plus a Paseo host that coordinates role agents.

architecture.text: Settings map configured code repositories to separate memory repositories under a coordination root. The tool server resolves repository identity from settings, rejects repositories not listed there, and writes MCP call logs under the coordination root or task enclosure.

The memory repository's Git-versioned text tree is canonical: Markdown onboarding cards, JSON sidecars with citations/realizations/proofs, route overviews, JSON knowledge records and Curator history files. Records have stable IDs, origins, statuses and revisions.

SQLite is a derived index rather than canonical storage. The inspected index schema includes repository, invariant/revision, family/revision, membership, source-anchor and realization-claim tables; record decoding verifies stored revision digests, and malformed inputs are represented as index problems rather than guessed.

behavior.text: The Curator authors semantic content in a hand-off list. The knowledge writer supplies IDs, source anchors, revisions, origin and history-row bindings, validates the write, and can plan or write files. The MCP writer does not make a Git commit; Git provides the surrounding history.

Records are not physically deleted through the documented knowledge model; a record leaves active use through status retired. Validation requires records present in the comparison base to remain in the candidate tree, so retirement does not erase Git history.

read_ar_files names card locations and records governing up to 20 requested code paths. knowledge_read selects typed views of records and returns IDs, states and file locations rather than record text; large selections are paged with a continuation bound to the same selection and snapshot.

Currentness is computed against the requested code commit or working tree by comparing recorded anchors; the repository presents code currentness and the record state but does not thereby certify semantic correctness.

Scope is selected by configured repository and task worktree roots. This is repository/task context routing, not evidence of authenticated tenant isolation; shared-host or multi-user authorization was not tested.

Origin and history associate authored knowledge with tasks or foundation waves, hand-off entries and evidence. Sidecars connect citations, code realizations and test proofs to records. These links support traceability but do not prove a recorded assertion is true or that a test covers every claim.

Source-visible bounds include at most 20 paths in read_ar_files and 32 items by default per knowledge_read page, with continuations for larger selections and a token threshold. The index builder memoizes parsed documents by content SHA within a process; MCP logs and reports expose counts, refusals and validation findings. These are implementation/documentation observations, not performance or completeness results.

metrics.evidence: The reviewed interfaces select and name records and cards; no answerability or abstention workload was run.
Revision history, currentness checks and retirement are visible in source; no correction or stale-value probes were run.
The documented model retires records and preserves prior Git history; no deletion-leakage probes were run.
Repository selection and task-scoped roots are visible in source and docs; no cross-scope or multi-user probes were run.
Citation sidecars, anchors, realization/proof links and provenance are visible; claim support and citation coverage were not adjudicated.
Reads use a derived index and bounded pages; no latency distributions or write-to-recall delay measurements were collected.
The system exposes bounded responses and uses a derived SQLite index; no token, cost, or storage measurements were collected.
Path/page limits, parse caching, MCP call logs and structured reports are visible. They do not establish runtime efficiency or observability coverage.

limits.text: This is a bounded inspection of the official README, architecture and knowledge-system references, plus selected current code at the verified full SHA. The product, tests and benchmarks were not run.

Repository and task scope selection do not establish tenant authorization or secure multi-user deployment. Retirement and Git history do not establish erasure from backups, exports or external systems.

Anchors and provenance help inspect where knowledge came from and whether referenced code changed; they cannot alone establish truth, answer quality or proof adequacy. Runtime behavior, performance and all benchmark outcomes remain unknown.

benchmark.text: Benchmark not run. No Agents Remember system, benchmark workload, or test suite was executed; no metric values were produced. Project metrics, fixture and shared status record describe protocol/status and are not results for this system.
